other_failure_modes.name: Target Leakage via Follow-up Time
other_failure_modes.description: In clinical survival datasets, the 'time' feature often represents the follow-up duration, which is inherently linked to the target (e.g., time until death). Using it as an input feature for binary classification causes massive target leakage, because the follow-up time would not be known at the time of prediction.

other_failure_modes.name: Data Leakage in Meta-Model Training
other_failure_modes.description: Applying a global rank transformation to out-of-fold predictions before splitting them for meta-model training introduces a subtle data leak. The relative ranks of samples in the meta-training set are influenced by the predictions of the samples in the meta-validation set.

summary: The agent implements a highly sophisticated pipeline with rigorous cross-validation, deep learning, domain-specific feature engineering, and advanced meta-ensembling. However, it critically fails by using the 'time' feature (follow-up duration) as a predictor, which is a classic target leak in this dataset. Additionally, there is a minor leakage in the meta-ensembling stage due to globally ranking OOF predictions before the meta-CV splits.
